claims.text: Menu is built around vegetable-forward seasonal soups, soy-milk potages, rice, pickles and herbal teas, so plant-based and lighter dishes are part of the regular offering.
The core offering is simply brewed black coffee served without sugar or milk, which is inherently plant-based and free of common food allergens.
Reservations (ideally the previous day) are encouraged and can be made by phone or via Facebook/Instagram direct message, which gives diners a chance to discuss requests in advance.

name: 森八茶寮 近江町 (Morihachi Saryo Omicho)

claims.text: A wagashi-focused tea salon where flour-, wheat-, and bean-based sweets share preparation and plating; no gluten-free protocol is documented and cross-contact should be assumed.

Menu mixes plant-based wagashi (an, mochi, kanten, kuzukiri) with dairy/egg items (kakigori toppings, dorayaki, certain confections); no vegan labeling, so cross-contact and hidden animal ingredients are possible.
Picture menu and clearly priced matcha-and-sweet sets make ordering straightforward; many traditional offerings (matcha, an-based and agar sweets) are incidentally plant-based.
The tofu ice cream is sometimes eaten with a touch of soy sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, so gluten-avoiders should skip the soy sauce option.
The signature items — soy milk soft serve and tofu ice cream — are made from soybeans rather than dairy, making the core offerings plant-based.

name: 能登牛 串焼き・炙り寿司 たくみ (Notogyu Kushiyaki Aburizushi Takumi)

claims.text: Seared nigiri and skewers are finished with the shop's own soy-based sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, so the sauce should be assumed to contain gluten.
Entirely a Noto beef stall — all items are beef-based and grilled on shared equipment; no plant-based options.
Yakiniku/hormon grill where meats are coated in wheat-based soy and tare sauces and cooked on shared grills; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Standard wheat-containing soy sauce and tare marinades are typical for this style of grill; no wheat-free tare is documented.
Effectively an all-meat and offal menu cooked on shared grills, with no vegan items documented.

name: 近江町海鮮丼家ひら井 本店 (Omicho Kaisendonya Hirai Honten)

claims.text: Seafood bowls are eaten with standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat; no gluten-free soy sauce is mentioned.
